source_label: IBM Granite blog on Hugging Face, "LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B"
notes: IBM Granite's LLM-native markup language, introduced with Granite 4.1 3B and 8B on 2026-11-12. The blog states the reading: LLMON (LLM Object Notation), pronounced "lemon". One word, not the letters L-L-M-O-N.

Thinking Machines Lab's small open-weights model, released 2026-11-20: a looped transformer that runs its middle layers three times per token. The launch post says nothing about the reading, so the entry follows Cambridge for the ordinary word: stress the first syllable, "INK-ling," not "ink-LING."

The company behind GeForce GPUs and CUDA, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Begin with the letter N and stress the second syllable: en-VID-ee-uh. The name comes from "invidia," the Latin word for "envy."
Alibaba's graph-native transactional database, open source under Apache-2.0 and on GitHub since 2026-03. Its README states the reading: NeuG (pronounced "new-gee"), "new" plus the letter G.
